lines:
Removed the Chat run-failure banner everywhere it was used and replaced it with the notice card commit 96c04c7 introduced for an interrupted reply.

Change: added ChatNoticeCard (desktop/src/chat/ChatNoticeCard.tsx) with one shell, one copy block and one action row. Both the interrupted-reply decision (warning accent, "Interrupted reply", Continue/Stop) and a terminal Run failure (danger accent, role=alert, Run details/Dismiss) render it. Renamed recovery.css to notice.css with neutral .chat-notice-* classes. ChatWorkspaceScreen renders the failure through ChatNoticeCard instead of a full-width `<div class="recovery-banner run-failure-banner">`, and the "Review" notification focuses the decision card explicitly instead of any first action row. Deleted the .recovery-banner/.recovery-actions CSS and the banner's grid-row rule from styles.css; no .recovery-banner, .run-failure-banner or .recovery-actions class remains under desktop/src.

Design: aworkit.desktop_ui.chat_notice_card linked to aworkit.desktop_ui.chat_workspace; the element now binds ChatNoticeCard.tsx and notice.css, and the stale recovery.css binding is removed.

Coverage: the stopped-Run test asserts the failure card (chat-notice-card--failure, role=alert, Run details, Dismiss) and that no .recovery-banner exists; the recovery test asserts the shared decision card. Verification: vitest src/chat 199 passed; full vitest run 524 passed across 70 files; tsc --noEmit clean.

Requirement (user, 2026-09-27): remove the run-failure banner everywhere it is used in the Chat and replace it with the card UI that commit 96c04c7 introduced for an interrupted reply.

Evidence: `.recovery-banner run-failure-banner` is the last use of `.recovery-banner` (ChatWorkspaceScreen.tsx ~L648-663; CSS in styles.css L575-579, L649-659, L663-675). 96c04c7 replaced only the `chat.recoveryPending` block with ChatRecoveryCard and left the terminal `execution.failed` banner unchanged, so a hard stop still uses the old full-width warning bar.

Acceptance:
1. No `.recovery-banner`, `.run-failure-banner` or `.recovery-actions` class remains anywhere under desktop/src (chat UI).
2. The terminal run failure renders through the same shared card as the interrupted reply, keeping title, body, Run details and Dismiss.
3. The hard stop is announced with role=alert; the interrupted-reply decision card keeps its region/aria-label semantics.
4. Existing recovery behaviour and its tests are unchanged.
5. A regression test asserts the failure card content and the absence of the old banner.
6. The design model states the Chat has one notice-card surface with decision and failure variants.

data.title: Replace the Chat run-failure banner with the notice card used for an interrupted reply
